messages.subject: Recovering data frames and complex R objects
messages.subject_clean: Recovering data frames and complex R objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm a new user of RServe, and I have a few doubts.
First of all, I've been able to create a simple Java R console that uses R with Rserve installed in a server.
I've been also able to create a REXPDecoder that converts REXP objects into Java data types using rexp.asInteger, rexp.asDoubles, rexp.asDoubleMatrix(), rexp.asStrings() and so on.

I wonder how can I do the same with data frames as it looks like Rserve interprets this data structure as only "bytes". Moreover, I wonder how can I inspect and convert into Java data structures complex R objects (those objects that contain more than one vector and matrix inside).

Any help will be much appreciated.
Thanks,

Victor

messages.body_plain:
On Dec 12, 2011, at 12:01 PM, Víctor Pascual Cid wrote:

> Hi all,
> 
> I'm a new user of RServe, and I have a few doubts.
> First of all, I've been able to create a simple Java R console that uses R with Rserve installed in a server.
> I've been also able to create a REXPDecoder that converts REXP objects into Java data types using rexp.asInteger, rexp.asDoubles, rexp.asDoubleMatrix(), rexp.asStrings() and so on.
> 
> I wonder how can I do the same with data frames as it looks like Rserve interprets this data structure as only "bytes".

That's not true, data frames are simply lists.


> Moreover, I wonder how can I inspect and convert into Java data structures complex R objects (those objects that contain more than one vector and matrix inside).
> 

The client actually does that already. The REXP methods you mentioned above are just accessor methods, the contents are already Java native types stored in the REXP as they come back. I suspect that you just didn't consider lists (generic vectors) which are the basic recursive structures in R.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Creating data.frames with JRI
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Using the JRI API, what's the right way to create a data.frame in R, from a List in Java ? I tried following Oliver Mannion's design pattern in jamsim of creating column arrays and doing rList.put() but the API has changed, and the constructor for RList he used no longer exists, and either does the put method for an RList object.

Say that I already have my columns in Java arrays :

String[] colNames = {"chr", "position"};
String[] chrs = {"chr1", "chr2", "chr3"};
Integer[] pos = {1000, 2000, 5000};

How do I get from there to a data.frame using the instance of Rengine I have created ?

--------------------------------------
Dario Strbenac
Research Assistant
Cancer Epigenetics
Garvan Institute of Medical Research
Darlinghurst NSW 2010
Australia

messages.body_plain:
Actually, I have forgotten about REXP.createDataFrame() - it creates the extra attributes for you - so it's even easier:

REXP df = REXP.createDataFrame(new RList(new REXP[] { new REXPString(chrs), new REXPInteger(pos) }, colNames));
eng.assign("df", df);
eng.parseAndEval("print(df)");

.. and in fact it's in one of the examples in RTest.java ...
  
Cheers,
Simon

http://rforge.net/org/doc/org/rosuda/REngine/package-summary.html

org.rosuda.REngine is the recommended high-level API that works for both JRI and Rserve. It's easier and safer to use. The org.rosuda.JRI API is the low-level API and you need to be a little more careful with it. But it should make no difference here. Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Suggested features
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I've been using RStudio for a while and now I'm back to using JGR. The combination of JGR and Deducer looks like the best way to enable our non-programming students to take advantage of R.  However, there are a few features that I miss. I hope the developers will consider adding these to a future version of JGR.

1. I often work on several programs at once, and RStudio's ability to automatically re-open all the files I previously had open is a big time saver. 

2. When teaching, I often use the mouse to select code and click RStudio's "run the current line or selection" toolbar icon. That lets me walk around the room with a remote control and not have to return to the keyboard as often.

3. In most applications, I copy or cut text using the right-click menus which don't appear in JGR. This might be a Windows-specific thing, but it sure comes in handy. Once the text is selected, CTRL-C and -X work fine, but right-clicking just cancels the selection. 

Thanks for making such great software!

Bob
